goal: Per-sheet isolation for a corrupt Excel sheet (Board gate 171: BUILD AC-25 per-sheet isolation this round): a workbook with one corrupt sheet still lists and opens its other sheets, and the corrupt one goes to Unreadable with its sheet name
criteria: app/xlsx.py `_load(path, keep=None)` copies the zip into a BytesIO and writes every xl/worksheets/*.xml part (not _rels) as an empty `<worksheet ...><sheetData/></worksheet>`, except the part named by `keep`, then calls openpyxl load_workbook(read_only=True, data_only=True); not a zip, no workbook part or any open error still raises ReadError('not a valid xlsx')

`sheet_names(path)` loads with every sheet blanked, so a workbook whose sheet 'Bad' is b'<<not xml' or truncated XML returns all sheet names in order (e.g. Good, Bad, Also); an empty list still raises 'not a valid xlsx'

`read_sheet(path, sheet)` finds the sheet's part, reloads with keep=that part and reads as before: Good and Also return their header and rows (a date cell stays a datetime) and Bad raises ReadError('not a valid xlsx')

`path` may be a path or a BytesIO (a BytesIO is seeked back to 0 before each copy); `_worksheet_path` use carries a `ponytail:` comment naming the private attribute and the openpyxl 3.1.5 pin, and a second one names the N+1 zip copies

New test in tests/test_xlsx_read.py using conftest.write_xlsx with a bytes sheet: for both b'<<not xml' and a truncated sheet XML, sheet_names lists all three sheets, Good and Also read, Bad raises 'not a valid xlsx'

A catalog scan of a folder holding that workbook lists Good and Also as datasets and one Unreadable 'book3.xlsx - Bad' with reason 'not a valid xlsx' (sheet field 'Bad'); the workbook alone is not in the unreadable list (test in tests/test_catalog.py)

Existing tests/test_xlsx_read.py::test_broken (not a zip -> 'not a valid xlsx'), tests/test_catalog.py::test_failed_sheet_is_listed_with_its_name and the header-less sheet case of test_AC_25 still pass unchanged; no edit to tests/test_acceptance.py (QA owns it)

goal: Launcher picks the newest Python 3.11-3.13 and fails cleanly when there is none (Board gate 171: accept 3.11-3.13 only, 3.14 rejected; message 'DataBoot needs Python 3.12. Install it with: winget install -e --id Python.Python.3.12', pause, exit 1)
criteria: Start-DataBoot.ps1 defines `function Fail($Message)` that does Write-Host $Message, then `if (Test-Path .venv) { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .venv }`, then Read-Host (to pause), then `exit 1`, in that order
One line `$Candidates = @(@("py", "-3.13"), @("py", "-3.12"), @("py", "-3.11"), @("python"))` holds the versions in that order; the script has no literal `py -3.1x -m venv` line

The script holds `$Check` = `import sys; sys.exit(0 if (3, 11) <= sys.version_info[:2] <= (3, 13) else 1)`; a loop skips a candidate when Get-Command (with -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) finds nothing, runs the check on every candidate including py ones (so 3.14 is rejected), with `$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"` set locally and restored (or try/catch) so py's stderr 'No suitable Python runtime' does not throw in Windows PowerShell 5.1; the first candidate with $LASTEXITCODE -eq 0 is used

The venv is created with `& $py[0] @rest -m venv .venv` on the chosen candidate; when none matches the script calls `Fail "DataBoot needs Python 3.12. Install it with: winget install -e --id Python.Python.3.12"` (exact text)
The folder dialog, folder check, -Docker branch, wheels install and final `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m app.launch $Folder` lines are unchanged

tests/test_launcher_files.py: replace the needle "py -3.11" with "-3.11" (every other needle stays) and add text tests: -3.13, -3.12, -3.11 appear in that order inside the `$Candidates` line followed by "python"; the script contains `(3, 11) <= sys.version_info[:2] <= (3, 13)`; `re.search(r"py -3\.1\d+ -m venv", ps1)` does not match; the exact no-Python message is present; `function Fail` holds Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .venv, Read-Host and exit 1 in that order
There is no PowerShell in the image, so the tests are text checks only; the Board runs the script on Windows with 3.12 + 3.14 and with no suitable Python

goal: Launcher checks the exit code after venv creation and after BOTH pip installs, wheels and online (Board gate 171), with the same Fail path: message naming the step, delete partial .venv, pause, exit 1
criteria: In Start-DataBoot.ps1 directly after `-m venv .venv`: `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "Could not create the Python environment (.venv)." }`
Directly after the `--no-index --find-links wheels` pip install: `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "Could not install the packages from wheels." }`
Directly after the online `pip install -r requirements.txt`: `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "Could not install the packages (pip install -r requirements.txt)." }`
Every Fail call comes before the final `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m app.launch $Folder` line, so a failed step never reaches it; each message names its step
The pip install lines keep working when wheels\ exists or not, and nothing in the -Docker branch changes

tests/test_launcher_files.py text tests: splitting the script at `-m venv .venv`, at `--find-links wheels` and at the online `pip install -r requirements.txt`, the text after each (up to the next native command) contains `$LASTEXITCODE -ne 0` and `Fail`; the last `Fail` position is before the `-m app.launch` position
